competitive_landscape: Access today splits between thin scheduled prop flights (1–2/day via Kendari or Makassar), a private resort charter flight from Bali for high-end guests, and a 10–12 hour overnight Pelni ferry for everyone else; on-island movement runs on local boats and resort tenders. It works, but it is slow, weather-exposed, and entirely undifferentiated — a striking mismatch with a destination this premium. That mismatch between a world-class reef and a basic, diesel-bound transit layer is precisely the opening for a clean, fast, quiet network.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The natural all-electric core: every inter-island hop — Wangi-Wangi↔Kaledupa ~10 nm, ↔Tomia ~25 nm, ↔Binongko ~45 nm — sits inside the 70 nm envelope, with Half-Foil/Shallow-Mode designed for the world-class reef-pass and lagoon geometry. Quiet-mode, low-wake operation suits the national park and Bajau stilt-village courtesy zones.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The mainland line-hauls: Kendari ~75 nm (edge of all-electric, comfortable on Quanta-LR), the Makassar super-hub ~280 nm, the Bau-Bau / Buton heritage run ~140 nm, and the seasonal phinisi-circuit stitch toward the Banda Islands ~250 nm. Hybrid range with no charging dependency fits island microgrids; Pertamina Kendari and Makassar support diesel refuel.

precedents.what: $100M, ~100-vessel phased electric-foiling network with JIH Global
precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a remote, high-value dive/charter archipelago adopting a clean-foiling network at scale — directly transferable to Wakatobi's resort-and-liveaboard demand.

regulatory_note: Triple environmental-channel oversight — Wakatobi National Park (KLHK/BB-KSDA), the UNESCO MAB Biosphere coordination, and KKP marine-reserve overlay — plus Kemenhub/DGST + BKI on the transport side. The park's year-round quota framework and biosphere status make a zero-emission, low-wake, quiet-mode fleet a clean fit, and reef-pass navigation discipline is a first-tier product-design input rather than a constraint.
seasonality: Dry, calm season runs roughly April–November (core June–September), with the dive peak spanning March–December; the wet, windier NW-monsoon months (Dec–Mar) bring residual Banda Sea swell on the outer arcs. Equatorial and largely outside the typhoon track. The exposed outer-island hops and monsoon chop are where foiling's smoother, more reliable ride pays off, while the sheltered Wangi-Wangi harbour is a benign year-round demo corridor.
signature_routes: Wangi-Wangi ↔ Tomia (Wakatobi Dive Resort corridor) — Pioneer II
summary: Wakatobi — Wangi-Wangi, Kaledupa, Tomia and Binongko — is a UNESCO Man-and-the-Biosphere Reserve and national park with the highest recorded hard-coral diversity on earth. Premium guests reach it via thin air links through Kendari or Makassar, or a private resort charter flight from Bali; everyone else faces a 10–12 hour overnight Pelni ferry. Once there, the four islands sit a tidy 10–45 nm apart — perfect all-electric range — while the mainland gateways are a clean Quanta-LR line-haul. The diving is world-class; the getting-around is the gap.
tagline: The Coral Triangle's epicentre — a fly-in dive paradise still stitched together by overnight ferries and chartered prop planes.

use_cases.body: A smooth, quiet all-electric shuttle on the Wangi-Wangi↔Tomia resort corridor and out to the dive walls and Bajau stilt-villages — replacing deep-draft tenders with Half-Foil/Shallow-Mode reef-pass handling inside the biosphere.
